column8: Wed 18 Nov: 3a, one clause of prior art at most: the UK waiting habit named while it happened, with Hymans's own hindsight caveat in the same sentence; aggregate, so some triggers fired (row 9).
Wed 18 Nov: 3a background: the yields-will-rise-faster view failed for a decade, so a plan that takes no yield view cannot fail that way; pairs with row 11, which says it more exactly.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: names the waiting habit in plain words; never a second image beside pencil and ink; an LDI seller's paper.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a, the best one-clause source for buying on a date: the XPS chief investment officer's words re-read at source today, word for word; pensions' time-based plans were staged over years, Laura's is one date, and never say the team chose this for that reason (row 48).
Wed 18 Nov: store: three families of hedging rule, Laura's the date family at its simplest; Mercer page undated and the small-plan point second-hand.

Wed 18 Nov: store, claim 1's correction: written triggers were a minority and fair-value waiting the common form; Aon's PDF refused a re-read today (robots), so the card's reading stands unchecked by this rater.
Wed 18 Nov: 3a, a sharp test of a rule: a fair-value target moved with the market, a date cannot; fix the page locator (p. near Chart 23) before any APA entry.
Wed 18 Nov: store: 20% of schemes with formal triggers in 2013, sitting about 10% of funding below them; never quote the article's 4 in 10 hit triggers headline, which its text does not explain.
Wed 18 Nov: store, claim 1's second correction: triggers set 10 or 20 basis points above the market did fire; undated page, drop its 30 per cent hedge ratio line.
Wed 18 Nov: the forward-curve point in trade-press words; row 11 is the regulator's version and stronger.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a aha candidate: waiting pays only if rates rise faster than the market already prices, so a wait is a bet against the forward curve and a date takes no view; footnote 45 re-read at source today, Dutch wording matches; say it in plain English with the translation.
Wed 18 Nov: store: slow reversion is why a waiting rule can wait a decade; Dutch hedge levels about 40% weighted, 60% unweighted at end-2014; two ideas in one row, Dutch liabilities on swaps.

Wed 18 Nov: store, the only written trigger schedule found (PMA, 2014); fix the use column: at today's rates most of each payment is owned from January 2027 and all ten from January 2028 (the top-up, NUMBERS 1), so never 100% of the ten from day one at any yield.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the Dutch adviser's version of the UK lesson; undated (file name suggests January 2020), read in part.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e honest counter or store: a 25-year Dutch back-test with 2022 inside it still found the waiting ladder added nothing; quotes re-read at source today; add the authors' own reason, a term premium, and say one ladder design on Dutch swap rates.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the largest Dutch fund cut its hedge to 22% near the bottom of rates; record the thesis author before any citation; ABP was back at 49.1% by end-2024 (Q73-024).
Wed 18 Nov: 3a, a US adviser beside the UK and Dutch record (a tactical under-hedge rarely beats the strategic hedge); web extract only, so quote only the two phrases on the card.
Wed 18 Nov: store, the dated yield path behind the trap; every monthly value re-read on FRED today and matches; monthly averages of the 10-year, not the long gilts many triggers used.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a sizing of a decade: run lengths below 2%-4.5% reproduced exactly today on the FRED series (82, 96, 133, 135, 149, 177 months); Keel arithmetic on monthly 10-year data, never a register figure.
Wed 18 Nov: store detail behind row 19: 0.5-point triggers 25 within a year, 9 never, median 93 months; 1-point 6, 33, 104; reproduced exactly today.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a, the answer to why not wait for better yields: over 1962-2025 a buy-higher-or-after-a-year rule averages about zero (-0.015, +0.001, +0.008 point), reproduced exactly today on the repo DGS10; yield points only, interest while waiting ignored, never says the date buys cheaper.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3c aha candidate (wins often and small, loses rarely and big); the yield figures reproduce exactly, but $14,800 and $28,300 are rough linear Keel arithmetic on NUMBERS 1's $300 a basis point, not register figures: say it in yield points or register the dollars first.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a support for taking no view: the 0.5-point rule gained +0.30 point in 1962-80 and lost 0.18 in 1981-2020, reproduced today; eras are chosen after the fact, so say nobody knows which one 2027 is in.
Wed 18 Nov: store: US starts 2010-2015 with no deadline waited a median 2.2 years (0.5 point) and 7.0 (1 point), reproduced today; Laura has the 2028 deposit and the 2031 meetings first.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 2.5, twin of NUM-007 and NUM-009 with a trigger framing; say a rule to buy only when $300,000 buys all ten, never a flat 5.02% (19 Oct 2023 was on the full curve, 10-year 4.98%); about 16 years is Keel arithmetic, not in 8e; drop might still be waiting (37 closes under $300,000 in 2026, 8b); AHA row 3's fixes apply.
Wed 18 Nov: 3a background: by 2016 the regulator itself told schemes relying on yield reversion to act; read from a mirror copy, so cite TPR's own archived copy before APA.
Wed 18 Nov: store disanalogy: a pension sponsor tops up year after year, Laura only once (IPS l.13); UNVERIFIED, TPR's 2015 text read only through LCP, so read it at source before any use.
Wed 18 Nov: store: TPR 2019's scorecard of the waiting years; UNVERIFIED, second-hand through Sackers.
Wed 18 Nov: store or 3a background: the government's own account blamed unhedged falls in gilt yields; overlaps rows 1 and 26, so one of them at most in the report.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the reversion forecast survived inside government to 2017; right on level, wrong on path (the 10-year passed 4% in Oct 2022).
Wed 18 Nov: 3a contrast: the lifeboat hedged while the schemes it insures often did not; say which deficit measure (aggregate £413bn, or schemes in deficit £451.1bn), never both as one.

Wed 18 Nov: store: why under-hedging hurt (liabilities up about 2.0% per 0.1 point, assets 0.7%); fix the use column: the instruments held move $234 a basis point against the payments' $300 (NUMBERS 1), so the ten do not move one for one; the extra Treasuries cover the gap.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2) store: a wait could only add exposure after the money lands (Q98 rows 6 and 26 checked: $23,560, $7,065, $57,034); rough Keel arithmetic comparing a one-year wait with an eight-week window, so say the direction only, never the $28,300 against $23,560.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3c, one shape in two places; 8c checked against NUMBERS and its 2026-11-17 file: rival ahead 59.8% house, 68.4% history, under $95,000 in 16.4% and 9.4%, re-sized figures; the payments half rests on row 22, so state it in yield points.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a candidate: IPS l.9's career reason also argues for the date; UNVERIFIED inference (CANON B4: her income is not observed); say the losing years can come in the same downturns, never bets against her career twice.
Wed 18 Nov: store, part of Q68's gap on UK hedging over time; CONFLICTING (£657bn against £675bn in one article) and KPMG's own PDFs unread, so no figure leaves the store until read at source.
Wed 18 Nov: store: most UK schemes reached high hedges only after 2019; samples differ by year; the 85% by 2022 is store Q2a-006's Work and Pensions Committee figure, not Aon's.
Wed 18 Nov: store: a third of LDI mandates had an extension trigger in 2013; UNVERIFIED, secondary German trade report of a KPMG survey.
Wed 18 Nov: store: UK advisers kept saying stop waiting; Barnett Waddingham still suggested triggers with stop-losses, so never quote it as against triggers.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e honest counter: TPR 2023 says unhedged schemes gained in 2022; sentences re-read at source today; the 160 basis points is already Q2a-001, so the new part is TPR's own sentence and its twelve-year delay.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a illustration of waiting as a two-way bet (80% hedge holds, 50% swings 85% or 76%); fix the use column: never Laura's ten are the 100% row, since most of each payment is owned from January 2027 and all ten from January 2028, and the held instruments' duration is shorter (NUMBERS 1); confirm the letter's author before citing.
Wed 18 Nov: the same 2022 counter-case from anecdotal adviser evidence; row 40 carries it at the regulator's source.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, one clause at most: the 2010s waiting and the 2022 borrowing were two answers to a hedge bigger than the cash; say Laura's ten are paid from her own deposits with no borrowing, not that the hedge equals the first deposit ($302,287 against $300,000, NUMBERS 1).
Wed 18 Nov: the hedge was right and its financing broke is H7-037's point; Breeden's incentive line and the £40 billion raised stay as detail there.
Wed 18 Nov: the standing buffer as the price of borrowing to hedge; Q3b-023 holds the regulator's 250bp version.
Wed 18 Nov: store: hedges rose after 2022 (XPS clients +3%, small schemes +16%); one adviser's clients, and the rise is not shown to be triggers firing, so drop the triggers did work as written.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: Dutch swap hedges carry margin-call liquidity risk; abstract read only, and Laura holds no derivatives, so it serves no part.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f guard: the catch quote checked in PEOPLE_IN_THE_ROOM Moment A; the moment itself is already SKELETON 3f (1), so the new value is the guard: no record shows the team weighing a wait, never write we chose not to wait.
Wed 18 Nov: 8b's fills and luck of timing (37 of 214 closes, checked) are NUM-003 and NUM-004 already.
Wed 18 Nov: restates CANON A34 and Table 3's row (Treasury yields and share prices: any level, no action); the for-scale cell is a 1-point fall, not the 10-year, so fix that wording if used.
